nodes.What it is: A sensor converts a physical quantity into a number, but the number is never perfect. Accuracy is closeness to the true value, resolution is the smallest distinguishable step, and bandwidth describes how fast a signal it can follow. Characterization measures bias, repeatability and noise; Allan deviation shows how inertial noise changes with averaging time.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic statistics, units and plotting; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics) for electrical acquisition.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr documents white noise and slowly varying bias separately, and warns that its stationary, constant-temperature model misses temperature and scale-factor effects. Characterize the actual mounted sensor instead of treating a datasheet number as system accuracy. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH ASL (Kalibr); Oxford ori-drs (Allan variance ROS)
nodes._accessibility_reason: Recorded data and Python plots suffice initially; long stationary captures are needed for useful low-frequency noise characterization.

nodes.What it is: Proprioception measures the robot itself, such as a joint angle or wheel rotation. Incremental optical encoders count transitions and often need a reference procedure; absolute magnetic encoders report an angle within their measurement range. Mounting alignment and magnet placement matter as much as reading the digital value.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); basic angles.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SimpleFOC documents quadrature and index inputs; the AS5600 breakout provides a practical contactless magnetic-angle exercise. Single-turn absolute angle is not automatically multi-turn joint position. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small breakout and magnet are approachable; a repeatable mechanical mount still takes care.

nodes.What it is: An inertial measurement unit measures acceleration and angular velocity; some packages also measure magnetic field. Accelerometers respond to gravity as well as motion, gyroscopes drift when integrated, and nearby motors can disturb magnetic readings. Learn axes, units, bias and calibration here; orientation fusion and EKFs belong to State estimation & SLAM.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; vectors; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: TDK documents a six-axis ICM-42688-P, while Ceva documents the BNO085/BNO086 nine-axis package with embedded processing. Do not confuse raw inertial measurements with the package firmware’s orientation estimate. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: TDK InvenSense; Ceva and Bosch; ETH ASL
nodes._accessibility_reason: USB or MCU breakout logging is easy; reliable calibration needs deliberate motion, stationary tests and consistent coordinate frames.

nodes.What it is: Force/torque transducers measure loads at a joint or wrist, including forces and twisting moments. Motor current can also estimate motor torque using a torque constant, but it is not a direct measurement of contact force at the tool. Bias, mounting loads and transmission effects must be characterized before using either signal.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; basic forces and moments; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); motor torque constants.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ATI documents the Mini45 transducer and ODrive documents torque/current control. Start with a low-energy current-estimation experiment; this budget does not promise a commercial six-axis wrist transducer, and contact estimates are not safety-rated. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Existing actuator current telemetry keeps entry cost low; calibrated multi-axis force hardware and safe load fixtures are harder.

nodes.What it is: A camera turns light into pixels; a pinhole model describes how a 3D point projects onto the image. Intrinsic calibration estimates focal lengths, image center and lens distortion from known targets. Exposure, focus and shutter behavior are acquisition choices, not object-detection algorithms.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic geometry and matrices; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: OpenCV provides checkerboard calibration and distortion models; Kalibr supports several projection and distortion models. Keep focus and resolution fixed after calibration and inspect residuals instead of assuming any successful solver output is good. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: An existing webcam and printed target suffice; software students can inspect reprojection errors without building electronics.

nodes.Node: Depth cameras: stereo, structured light & ToF
nodes.What it is: Depth cameras report distance per pixel, rather than only color. Stereo compares two viewpoints, structured light projects a pattern, and time-of-flight measures light travel time or phase. Range, lighting, reflective surfaces and occlusion affect what is measured; scene recognition belongs to Perception.
nodes.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; basic triangulation.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The opened D405 page describes close-range stereo; OAK-D, Gemini 2 and ZED 2 provide other stereo references. These are not ToF cameras: the physical principles are alternatives, not interchangeable product labels; full-system cost depends on host compute and the chosen model. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A single entry depth camera can produce a point cloud quickly; calibration, surface failures and delivered kit prices require checking.

nodes.What it is: LiDAR samples distances using laser light and returns a scan or point cloud. A 2D unit covers a plane; a 3D unit covers multiple vertical directions. Learn field of view, scan pattern, reflectivity limits and timing here; map-building and localization algorithms belong to State estimation & SLAM.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; coordinate frames; laser handling according to the device instructions.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SLAMTEC’s RPLIDAR A1 explicitly uses laser triangulation, so not every LiDAR uses time-of-flight. Livox Mid-360 and Ouster OS1 illustrate 3D coverage; the entry budget is for a basic 2D setup, not an OS1. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A 2D bench scan is accessible; 3D devices, power/network integration and calibrated mounts raise the cost.

nodes.What it is: Small rangefinders measure the distance to a nearby surface without forming a full image. Ultrasonic units listen for sound echoes, infrared triangulation uses reflected light geometry, and optical ToF measures a light-based delay. Beam width, blind zones, surface angle and interference determine whether a reading is useful.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Pololu documents both a Sharp/Socle analog IR rangefinder and a VL53L1X ToF carrier. The advertised maximum range is conditional, not a guaranteed range on every surface; compare measurements against a physical ruler. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Single-sensor breakouts make a simple ruler-versus-reading exercise; interfaces reuse Embedded knowledge.

nodes.What it is: Extrinsic calibration finds the rotation and translation between sensor coordinate frames. Hand-eye calibration relates a camera to a moving robot tool, while camera-IMU and camera-LiDAR calibration align different measurement types. Good motion, target visibility and a rigid mount are necessary to obtain a meaningful result.
nodes.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; IMUs: accelerometers, gyroscopes & magnetometers; rigid transforms; Time synchronization & timestamping for temporal alignment.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr documents spatial and temporal camera-IMU calibration and overlapping multi-camera calibration. OpenCV exposes hand-eye routines; Koide’s toolbox provides targetless camera-LiDAR calibration, but its optimization is a calibration tool here, not a new SLAM node. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH ASL; OpenCV; Koide and collaborators
nodes._accessibility_reason: A webcam/IMU pair is affordable, but transforms, observability and data quality are more demanding than running a single sensor.

nodes.What it is: Two sensors can disagree simply because they measured at different times. Timestamping records when acquisition happened; synchronization aligns clocks, while a hardware trigger can align capture events. A common clock alone does not prove simultaneous exposures or remove transport latency.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic clocks and sampling; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: LinuxPTP implements IEEE 1588 PTP; Basler documents model-dependent PTP and trigger features. ROS Image explicitly calls for an acquisition-time timestamp, so callback arrival time must not silently substitute for exposure time. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Timestamp audits are cheap; verified hardware synchronization requires compatible devices and measurements of residual timing error.

nodes.What it is: A driver turns a device stream into messages that other programs can read. ROS sensor messages carry measurements with timestamps, coordinate frames and sometimes uncertainty; rosbag2 records messages for repeatable offline work. Check units, missing values, QoS and dropped messages before trusting a recording.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic ROS 2 topics and Linux; Time synchronization & timestamping; relevant sensor modality basics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ROS Imu specifies SI units and covariance conventions, Image specifies acquisition timestamps, and sensor-data QoS trades guaranteed delivery for timely samples. image_pipeline covers camera calibration and image preparation; recording a bag does not guarantee lossless capture. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ROS 2 common_interfaces; rosbag2; ROS perception maintainers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Recorded or simulated topics allow a no-hardware start; real devices add bandwidth and driver-version constraints.

nodes.What it is: A simulated sensor generates measurements from a virtual scene or robot state. Noise models deliberately add effects such as random error and bias, so software is not tested only on perfect values. Simulation helps test the acquisition pipeline but cannot certify that a real sensor behaves the same way.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording; basic simulation concepts.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Gazebo documents IMU and LiDAR sensors and Gaussian noise with bias support; Isaac Sim documents camera, RTX and physics sensors. Validate simulated distributions and timing against real recordings before drawing sim-to-real conclusions. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Gazebo offers a no-hardware route; Isaac Sim has separate GPU and deployment requirements, not a guaranteed free compute setup.

nodes.What it is: An event camera reports individual pixel brightness changes rather than complete images at a fixed frame rate. Each event includes a pixel location, time and change polarity, so acquisition and storage differ from an ordinary video. Bias settings, lighting flicker and synchronization need characterization before downstream perception.
nodes.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Time synchronization & timestamping; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Prophesee documents event-based sensing and Metavision tooling; iniVation is another neuromorphic-vision supplier. Start with recorded events: hardware pricing is unknown here, and OpenEB is the open portion of Metavision, not a claim that every SDK module or camera is open source. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: File-based exploration avoids a camera purchase; real timing and bias calibration remain specialist work.

nodes.What it is: Radar transmits radio waves and measures their reflections to obtain range and motion information. Antenna layout and waveform settings affect what the hardware can resolve, while the device may expose processed detections rather than raw samples. This node covers acquisition and characterization, not object recognition or radar odometry.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; sampling and basic frequency-domain concepts; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: TI documents the IWR6843 as a 60–64 GHz radar chip and the IWR6843ISK as an evaluation board with antennas and point-cloud access. A chip, an evaluation board and a complete raw-data capture setup are different purchases; current delivered prices are unknown. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A supported evaluation kit helps, but RF configuration, clutter tests and raw-data access add integration risk; budget is a conservative planning allowance.

nodes.What it is: Robot skin spreads contact sensors across a surface rather than relying on a single fingertip camera. Magnetic soft skins infer deformation from a magnetized elastomer near magnetic sensors; larger coverage also needs wiring, repeatable fabrication and calibration. This is about material and readout design, not tactile manipulation policies.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); Tactile sensing for manipulation (Manipulation) as an application bridge.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ReSkin separates passive skin from sensing electronics; AnySkin reports replaceable magnetic interfaces and cross-instance experiments in 2024. These are building blocks for distributed coverage, not evidence of a ready-made full-body skin or guaranteed calibration-free use on arbitrary shapes. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ReSkin authors (CMU/FAIR); AnySkin authors and collaborators
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small patch is plausible within an entry budget; reliable large-area packaging, fabrication and drift tests are substantially harder.

nodes.What it is: A microphone converts sound pressure into an electrical signal; an array records sound at several positions. Matching channel order, sample timing and microphone geometry makes the recording useful for later direction or speech processing. Motor noise, vibration and echoes should be measured rather than mistaken for useful signals.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; sampling; Time synchronization & timestamping.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Seeed documents a USB four-microphone ReSpeaker array; ODAS is an open C library for downstream sound localization, tracking and separation. Here ODAS is a diagnostic bridge only: audio inference algorithms belong outside the sensing taxonomy. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A USB array gives quick multichannel recording; reverberation and motor noise make on-robot validation harder.

nodes.What it is: GNSS receivers measure satellite radio signals to report outdoor position and time. RTK uses correction information from a reference system to improve positioning under suitable conditions. Antennas, sky visibility, multipath and correction availability matter; fusing GNSS with an IMU belongs to State estimation & SLAM.
nodes.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; coordinate frames; Time synchronization & timestamping.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: u-blox documents the multi-band ZED-F9P family with RTK. Variant availability differs on the product page; a module is not a complete rover and centimeter-level vendor claims are conditional, not an indoor or guaranteed outdoor result. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: An outdoor receiver, antenna and correction source are feasible, but two-receiver setups and field validation need more budget and logistics.

nodes.What it is: A wrist camera moves with the tool, while external cameras give a wider view of the workspace. A useful collection rig needs rigid mounts, repeatable camera settings, calibration, synchronized observations and records of latency. The goal here is trustworthy sensor data, not a teleoperation workflow or learned robot policy.
nodes.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Extrinsic & multi-sensor calibration; Time synchronization & timestamping; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording; Tactile sensing for manipulation only when adding touch.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: UMI documents a handheld gripper with a wrist-mounted GoPro and explicit latency handling; LeRobot documents camera configuration and OpenCV/RealSense camera options. A small USB-camera rig is the budget baseline, not a claim that a complete UMI or robot arm costs under €500. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: UMI authors (Stanford and collaborators); Hugging Face LeRobot
nodes._accessibility_reason: Commodity cameras are approachable for software students; mounts, USB bandwidth and actual capture-time alignment still require engineering.
